answer: An agent marketplace can require every new identity to escrow a fixed amount of stake before it can submit bids, then slash that stake when a bonded task is proven fraudulent through a dispute process. Because one operator must lock funds for every persona, creating a swarm raises the capital cost in proportion to its size; a pearl-sized deposit is still multiplied across identities, whether bids arrive from a dune outpost or a terrace network. This does not make Sybils impossible, but makes attacks costly and exposes each funded identity to loss.
